title: To direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
official_title: To direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
summary: This is a concurrent resolution invoking the War Powers Resolution to direct the President to pull U.S. Armed Forces out of Venezuela unless Congress has explicitly authorized their use through a declaration of war or a specific authorization for military force. It expresses the will of both chambers and does not change any law.
brief: Directs the President, under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Venezuela absent congressional authorization.

top_lines.headline: War Powers Directive on Venezuela
subs: Invokes section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution
Directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Venezuela
Exception only if authorized by a declaration of war or specific military-force authorization

likelihoodReason: The concurrent resolution failed in the House on January 22, 2026 on a 215-215 tie vote (a tie defeats the measure). Because it did not pass the House, it cannot proceed to the Senate, and the matter is effectively closed for this measure.

sections.label: Section 1 — Removal of the Use of United States Forces for Hostilities Within or Against Venezuela

items.main: Directs the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1544(c)), to remove United States Armed Forces from Venezuela.
items.detail: The directive applies unless the use of those forces is explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific statutory authorization for the use of military force. The resolution is a single operative section and contains no findings or additional provisions.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Deluzio
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, to respond to the notion of hypocrisy, that we should rely on the Secretary of State's notification when required, we were not notified--the Congress did not receive notification--or asked for authorization before Americans were sent to fight and to bleed in Venezuela. Seven Americans were wounded in that military operation. There is a functional blockade of Venezuelan oil.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Ryan
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, we face a fundamental question here: Who makes the decision to send our most precious resource, our young men and women in uniform, into harm's way? Is it a five-time draft dodger who has called them suckers and losers, or is it the American people with us as their voices? Mr. Speaker, I was on the receiving end of this same chicken-hawk bs for 27 months in combat in Iraq, and I don't need to be lectured by my colleagues.

gaps: The resolution directs removal of forces not authorized by Congress but does not state a deadline by which the President must complete the removal.
The resolution invokes the War Powers Resolution mechanism but does not specify which current U.S. military activities in or around Venezuela it considers unauthorized.
The resolution directs removal absent authorization but does not address forces engaged in self-defense or other activities not amounting to hostilities.
